decision: SECURITY POLICY FIXTURE PASS WITH STRICT RECOMMENDATIONS
scope: Encode the Phase 8S threat model and route inventory findings as machine-readable, test-enforced security policies. Policy definition only; no controls are implemented.

routeInventoryIntegration.note: The policy fixture test recomputes these counts from the route inventory fixture and requires exact agreement so the two fixtures cannot drift apart.

requirements: Wildcard origin ('*') must not be used together with credentials:true.
Production CORS must use an explicit origin allowlist.
A missing production allowlist must fail closed (deny), not default to wildcard.
Staging and production origins must be separately classified.
CORS policy must be tested before Phase 9.

notes: Content-Security-Policy applies where the backend returns renderable content.
Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) should be evaluated at the platform/proxy level, not necessarily in-app.
X-Frame-Options or a frame-ancestors CSP directive is required to prevent framing.

requirements: Public auth endpoints (/register, /login) require stricter rate limits and lockout policy.
Model/retrieval/mode routes require rate limits.
Admin/index routes require rate limits.
All expensive-operation routes require rate limits.
GET /health requires a rate limit because it performs a DB read via getVectorStoreStats.
Rate-limit policy must cover all 22 expensive-operation routes recorded in the route inventory.
Every route must appear in the route inventory.
Route inventory drift must fail tests.
Public routes must be explicitly classified public.
Authenticated routes must require authenticate.
Mode routes must require authenticate.
Admin/index/read/debug routes must require allowAuthenticatedOrIndexSecret or stronger.
An unknown guard is not acceptable for Phase 9 readiness.
Admin routes require an explicit admin_guard policy.
Debug routes require a debug_guard policy.
Debug/diagnostic route output must be minimized.
/routes and /health require a reconnaissance-minimization policy.
Admin/read/index routes require log_redaction and error_sanitization policy.
INDEX_SECRET or any admin-equivalent secret must not be accepted via URL query string in the future hardened state.
The future accepted path must be header-only or stronger.
Current query-string acceptance is recorded as a known risk (server.js getAdminSecret reads req.query.secret).
All admin routes are flagged no_query_secret in the route inventory.
P0 secrets must never be logged.
Required env vars must fail fast when missing.
Optional env vars must not silently enable insecure production fallbacks.
Production must not default to wildcard CORS.
No env values may be printed in reports, tests, or logs.
Logs touching request/answer content must pass through redaction in the future hardened state.
Production logs must not contain raw user queries or PII/client identifiers.
Langfuse / third-party egress requires a redaction and data-classification policy.
P1 data must not be sent to third-party observability without an approved policy.
Query/answer content must be classified and redacted before egress.
Third-party egress must be test-gated before Phase 9.
Production error responses must not expose raw error.message.
Production error responses must not expose stack traces.
Route catch blocks must eventually use a sanitizing helper/policy.
Diagnostic detail must be gated.
Tenant/client/matter isolation is mandatory before Phase 9.
User/client/matter data must be scoped.
Generated professional work product must be access-controlled.
Conversation routes touching user data require tenant_isolation.
Mode routes handling client facts require tenant_isolation.
PATCH-08S-TENANT-ISOLATION-GATE-1 is mandatory before Phase 9.

supabaseServiceRolePolicy.calibratedWording: Supabase service-role access may be acceptable only for tightly controlled server-only administrative/source-corpus operations. It is not acceptable as the default access path for user/client/matter data in Phase 9 without tenant-scoping, RLS, or an equivalent isolation model.
requirements: Service-role-as-default-path for user/client/matter data is a CRITICAL risk.
The future tenant isolation gate must define permitted service-role use.
No DB/Supabase changes occur in this patch.
User prompts must be treated as untrusted input.
User-provided instructions cannot override system/governance rules.
Prompt injection tests are required before Phase 9.
Generated professional documents must preserve source/authority discipline.
User-provided source references cannot create citations.
User-provided URLs/text cannot create source cards.
User-provided text cannot upgrade sourceAvailability or Authority Lock.
Authority remains controlled by the retrieval/source-card system, not by memory or user text.
Phase 10 source-governance remains deferred.
Request-size limits must be policy-controlled.
Expensive endpoints require stricter size/rate policy.
Auth endpoints require strict body expectations.
Generated document routes in Phase 9 require a size policy before implementation.
Public /routes and /health require a future minimization or gating policy.
Debug/internal metadata must not be exposed publicly in production.
Route banners must not advertise admin secret usage.
Memory remains inactive.
No TINA_ENABLE_MEMORY_* flags are enabled.
No persistent memory.
No runtime memory.
No memory DB/Supabase schema.
No memory route/pipeline/frontend integration.

phase8XDiagnosticSeparation.note: Short-term chat/session context carryover diagnostic; distinct from persistent memory and from Phase 8S security work.

prohibitedClaims: runtime security hardening is already implemented
CORS/headers/rate-limit are already enforced at runtime

testCases.expect: production CORS fails closed without allowlist
GET /health requires rate_limit due to DB read
route inventory drift must fail tests
unknown guard not acceptable for Phase 9
INDEX_SECRET via query prohibited in hardened state
P0/P1/P2, TIN, client_name, figures, raw prompts/answers redacted
user text cannot create citations/source cards/authority
